messages.author: c1f40f19e0a4bab0
messages.subject: boot.mirt
parts:
newbie question:

If I want to estimate the SE of IRT parameters, can I use boot.mirt?

For example I ran the following for a 14-item, 5-category response instrument, which has 70 parameters:
>mod_SC_P06<- mirt(data, 1, itemtype = "graded")

Then I ran the following:
>booted_SC <- boot.mirt(mod_SC_P06, R=40)
>booted_SC

Here are the first few lines of what it printed:
Bootstrap Statistics :
        original           bias                 std. error
t1*   0.70261210 -8.774317e-03   0.1515351
t2*   2.85604187  4.388296e-02   0.3718075
t3*   1.71292768  4.418255e-02   0.2283360
t4*   0.31787292  6.393808e-03   0.1796759

When I run mirt with pars='values' it shows that t1 = a1, t2 = d1, t3 =d2, etc

So, if the value of a1 that I extract by running:
coef(mod_SC_P06)
is 0.511, is it correct to say that a1 = 0.511 with an SE of 0.151?

Just making sure I'm interpreting this correctly!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: boot.mirt
parts:
Yes, boot.mirt() gives non-parametric SE estimates via the bootstrap method. Otherwise, you want parametric estimates, simply passing SE = TRUE to the estimation function will compute the standard errors based on the inversion of the information matrix. HTH.

Phil
